objective: Sub-goal B191 (the owner's second stage, coordinator's go-ahead 2026-11-17; goals G15, G16). A fast loop (re-tuned Novelty+) searches a planted not-all-equal knot pattern; between its epochs a slow loop reads where it dwelt and mutates the structure there with two moves that keep the allowed states: untangle (merge a tie class found by a bounded refutation) and braid (add a signed three-place knot, a shadow of the pattern that passes K1-K3). Charged work (incidences touched by both loops, rebuilds included) and CPU against the fast loop alone (best of re-tuned Novelty+ and probSAT, five runs per instance), static probing (the preprocessing precedent), random targets, an untangle-only ablation and CaDiCaL; the slow loop's policy is tuned on rand 2.1 and block 2.5 and tested on held-out local patterns (windows 10 and 40). Stop at the frozen rule.
title: Does a slow loop that mutates the knot structure, guided by where a fast search dwells, cut the charged work of solving unseen knot patterns, and does a mutation policy learned on some meeting patterns carry to others?
